nameOrigin.text: In 1894 David E. Severance applied for a post office for a community that was to be named Tailholt. Because he made the application, the post office was named Severance by mistake, and the name stayed.

founded.text: Founded by Bruce Eaton, son of Governor Benjamin Eaton

timeline.text: David E. Severance applied for a post office for a community of about 50 families.
The sugar factory in neighboring Windsor was built. Severance became a sugar beet receiving station and dump on the Great Western Railway.
Residents voted to incorporate, 40 for and 0 against.
The sugar beet receiving station on the Great Western Railway stopped operating.
